matrix: PLAN §49.4 Connectivity matrix and §49.7 Cluster matrix
note: Almost every case here needs hardware the CI host does not have: a second Spark, a QSFP cable, particular Wi-Fi topologies. Each is declared with the exact command and the evidence it must produce, so the gap is a stated prerequisite rather than an absence nobody records. Cases that a workstation can genuinely decide are mapped to tests.

blocked.reason: Needs the factory setup hotspot on a retail Spark, which exists only before first boot completes.
blocked.evidence_command: On a factory-reset Spark, from an iPhone: Settings > Wi-Fi, join the spark-* network, then run the app's Add Spark flow.
blocked.expected_evidence: The app joins without sending the user to Settings and reaches the provisioning stage; the onboarding model records connection before provisioning.

blocked.reason: Needs a real Wi-Fi network; the route logic itself is covered by routePriorityFollowsDefaultOrder.
blocked.evidence_command: With Spark and an iPad on one home Wi-Fi network: run the app's discovery and open the dashboard.
blocked.expected_evidence: Bonjour lists the node and GET /api/v1/status succeeds over the Wi-Fi route.

blocked.reason: Needs a wired LAN.
blocked.evidence_command: With Spark and a Mac on one switch: dns-sd -B _spark-runtime._tcp local. then open the dashboard.
blocked.expected_evidence: The node is discovered and the dashboard reports the wired route.

blocked.reason: Needs a Thunderbolt/USB-C Ethernet adapter and a direct cable (§13.4).
blocked.evidence_command: Mac and Spark cabled directly, then POST /api/v1/network/direct-profile with {"enabled": true} and a presence proof.
blocked.expected_evidence: The operation succeeds; the Spark holds 192.168.251.2/30 with no default route (ip route show | grep -c default is unchanged) and the Mac reaches https://192.168.251.2:7443/api/v1/health.

blocked.reason: Needs an iPhone with an active cellular plan and Personal Hotspot enabled.
blocked.evidence_command: Join the Spark to the iPhone hotspot, then run discovery from the same iPhone.
blocked.expected_evidence: The node is reachable; if mDNS is blocked on the hotspot the app falls back to the recorded route rather than failing silently.

blocked.reason: Needs a Wi-Fi adapter in AP mode on the Spark (§14).
blocked.evidence_command: POST /api/v1/network/travel-ap with {"enabled": true} and a presence proof, then join the advertised SSID from an iPad.
blocked.expected_evidence: nmcli connection show lists spark-travel-ap; the returned passphrase joins the network; https://192.168.252.1:7443/api/v1/health responds; existing LAN profiles are still present.

blocked.reason: Needs a network configured for client isolation.
blocked.evidence_command: Put Spark and iPad on an isolated guest network and run discovery.
blocked.expected_evidence: Discovery finds nothing and the app explains client isolation rather than reporting a generic failure.

blocked.reason: Needs a network with IPv6 disabled.
blocked.evidence_command: Disable IPv6 on the test network, then run discovery and open the dashboard.
blocked.expected_evidence: The node is reachable over IPv4 and no route candidate is left permanently pending on an unreachable IPv6 address.

blocked.reason: Needs an IPv6-capable link (§13.4 prefers link-local + Bonjour).
blocked.evidence_command: Cable Mac and Spark directly with no DHCP, then browse for the service.
blocked.expected_evidence: The link-local address is used and https://[fe80::...%25en0]:7443/api/v1/health responds.

blocked.reason: Needs a network that filters multicast.
blocked.evidence_command: Block UDP 5353 on the test network, then open a previously paired Spark in the app.
blocked.expected_evidence: The app reaches the node through its stored route and reports discovery as unavailable rather than the node as gone.

blocked.reason: Needs two physical interfaces on the client.
blocked.evidence_command: With the dashboard open and streaming, unplug Ethernet so the Mac falls back to Wi-Fi.
blocked.expected_evidence: The stream reconnects on the new route within the backoff window and the node identity is unchanged.

Local to Cloudflare failover..retired: Owner decision on 2026-09-05: public remote access was removed; Tailscale is the supported remote provider.

Cloudflare outage while local works..retired: Owner decision on 2026-09-05: public remote access was removed; Tailscale is the supported remote provider.

blocked.reason: Needs two Sparks and an approved QSFP cable.
blocked.evidence_command: With both nodes cabled: POST /api/v1/cluster/validate on the coordinator.
blocked.expected_evidence: The link probe reports the ConnectX interface up at >=100000 Mb/s with MTU 9000, and the cluster reaches ready.

blocked.reason: Needs two Sparks holding different model revisions.
blocked.evidence_command: Install different revisions of one model on each node, then POST /api/v1/cluster/create.
blocked.expected_evidence: Creation is refused naming the mismatched revision; neither node's local inference is disturbed.

blocked.reason: Needs a live two-node Ray cluster.
blocked.evidence_command: On the coordinator with a distributed model loaded: docker restart the Ray head container, then GET /api/v1/cluster.
blocked.expected_evidence: The cluster reports degraded, then ready once the head rejoins; in-flight requests fail with a retryable error rather than hanging.

blocked.reason: Needs two Sparks.
blocked.evidence_command: Start a distributed load, then unplug the QSFP cable before it completes.
blocked.expected_evidence: The load operation fails with a named error, the coordinator returns to a usable single-node state, and no partial engine is left running.

blocked.reason: Needs two Sparks.
blocked.evidence_command: During a streaming completion, unplug the QSFP cable.
blocked.expected_evidence: The stream terminates with an error the client can retry; the coordinator reports degraded and remains recoverable.

blocked.reason: Needs two Sparks.
blocked.evidence_command: Reboot the coordinator with a formed cluster, then GET /api/v1/cluster on both nodes.
blocked.expected_evidence: Both nodes agree on the cluster identity after restart and no operation is left running.

blocked.reason: Needs two Sparks and a partially replicated model.
blocked.evidence_command: Start replication over QSFP and interrupt it, then retry.
blocked.expected_evidence: The retry resumes from the content-addressed blobs already present rather than starting over, and the digest is verified before use.

blocked.reason: Needs two Sparks.
blocked.evidence_command: Leave the cluster once while idle and once during a generation.
blocked.expected_evidence: Both nodes return to standalone; the active case fails the in-flight request safely and leaves single-node inference usable.

blocked.reason: The app's wrong-password state is deterministic, but proving NetworkManager retained the previous live profile needs a Spark joined to two real access points.
blocked.evidence_command: On a Spark with a working saved WLAN, submit a wrong password for a second SSID through SparkPilot, then run nmcli -t -f NAME connection show --active.
blocked.expected_evidence: The app reports the password error and the prior WLAN remains active without waiting for the failsafe timer.

blocked.reason: The typed route, local UI, root-owned journal and 30-second timer are covered in process tests, but proving that NetworkManager restores a live DGX LAN profile needs a physical Spark and a second management route.
blocked.evidence_command: On a Spark reachable over both Wi-Fi and Ethernet, apply a valid but unreachable manual LAN/DNS candidate from SparkPilot, close the app without confirming, then watch nmcli connection show and ip route for 35 seconds.
blocked.expected_evidence: The old profile and route return automatically and no caller-supplied nmcli argument reaches spark-privd.

blocked.reason: Needs two paired Sparks and a 200 GbE QSFP cable to exercise both insertion orders.
blocked.evidence_command: Pair both Sparks, run discovery once with the cable already inserted and once inserting it while the cluster screen is open.
blocked.expected_evidence: Both orders produce the same authenticated link candidate and neither creates a cluster without owner confirmation.

blocked.reason: The current authenticated cluster model does not yet carry switch-versus-direct topology evidence into the Apple presentation layer.
blocked.evidence_command: Connect two paired Sparks through a supported fabric switch and inspect the cluster topology card.
blocked.expected_evidence: Both members appear in one cluster without a direct-cable line between them.

blocked.reason: The signed two-sided commit-receipt and finalize transaction is covered deterministically; proving both physical Sparks converge across real CX-7 timing requires the hardware pair.
blocked.evidence_command: With two Sparks, interrupt the second member after prepare and compare GET /api/v1/cluster on both nodes.
blocked.expected_evidence: Both nodes either report the same ready cluster ID or both remain standalone.

blocked.reason: Expiry reconciliation and rollback after an app exit between member commits are covered deterministically; process termination against two real Sparks remains the physical proof.
blocked.evidence_command: Terminate SparkPilot during prepare, restart the coordinator, then reopen the cluster on both members.
blocked.expected_evidence: The durable transaction resumes or rolls back without duplicate clusters or a half-joined member.

blocked.reason: The signed multi-node coordinator and retained grants are implemented; proving that a real import leaves Netplan, SSH, Ray, vLLM, models, containers and services byte-for-byte unchanged requires the physical cluster.
blocked.evidence_command: On an existing two-node Ray/vLLM cluster, choose Add Existing Cluster and diff Netplan, SSH, Ray, vLLM and model state before and after.
blocked.expected_evidence: SparkPilot records authenticated members and telemetry while every external configuration digest remains unchanged.

blocked.reason: Three-node ring topology validation is planned but not implemented and needs three Sparks plus three fabric links.
blocked.evidence_command: Try adding a third Spark first with two links, then with all three ring links present.
blocked.expected_evidence: The incomplete ring is refused; the complete authenticated ring becomes eligible.

blocked.reason: Four-node switched-topology validation is planned but not implemented and needs four Sparks plus a supported switch.
blocked.evidence_command: Try forming four direct peers, then repeat with all four connected to a supported fabric switch.
blocked.expected_evidence: The unsupported direct topology is refused and only the authenticated switched topology can proceed.
